title: The Salt Passage
premise: Theo Oyelaran has spent two decades as a freelance salvage diver and river pilot, outrunning the shadow of her mother, celebrated archaeologist Dr. Adaeze Oyelaran, whose last expedition ended in a scandal that cost Theo her name. When Adaeze's team goes silent upriver during the approach of an early monsoon, Theo is the only one who can navigate the flooded channels in time. She teams up with Imani, a disgraced former expedition medic with her own reasons to hate the project's financier, and together they uncover that the 'expedition' is a cover for looted artifacts being smuggled out under Adaeze's coerced signature. In the climax, Theo must choose between saving the artifacts or her mother as the river takes the camp; she saves both by sacrificing the boat, exposing the financier with evidence Imani kept hidden for years. The book ends with mother and daughter stranded on a shrine island through the monsoon, finally measuring life in days instead of miles.
about_author: Noor Okafor is a former river guide who spent six seasons working the delta waterways of West Africa before turning to fiction full-time. Her writing blends firsthand knowledge of monsoon-season rivers with a lifelong obsession with the ethics of archaeology.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Working a salvage job on the coast, Theo measures her life in distances traveled, never staying anywhere long enough to unpack. A telegram arrives: her estranged mother's expedition has gone silent upriver. Theo burns the telegram, then can't sleep. Emotional beat: the ache of a wound she pretends is healed.

chapters.title: The Debt of Water
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She tells herself she's going for the salvage fee, not for Adaeze. She charters passage to the last functioning river town, where officials refuse to send boats ahead of the storm season. She learns the expedition was funded by Halvard Voss, a collector with a reputation for buying silence. Beat: reluctant commitment disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Dock
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Imani watches Theo argue with boatmen and recognizes the stubbornness of someone chasing Voss's money trail — the same trail that destroyed Imani's medical career eight years ago. She offers her skills and half her savings. Beat: two guarded people recognizing each other's armor.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They buy the only affordable vessel, the Marrow, which leaks like a confession. First day upriver: rapids, a cracked seam, Theo diving under the hull in brown water to patch it while Imani bails. Beat: grudging respect born from shared labor.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At an abandoned trading post they find expedition gear dumped — radios, crates, a field journal page in Adaeze's handwriting, dated after the supposed silence. Someone wanted the world to think the team vanished. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Imani's Ledger
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Flashback woven into present: eight years ago, Imani documented Voss's men stealing finds from a dig site and was discredited when she reported it. She reveals why she really came — she kept copies of everything. Beat: trust extended as a test.

chapters.title: The First Monsoon Wind
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The sky turns the color of bruised fruit; the first squall hits early. They shelter in a fishing village where an old woman recognizes Adaeze's name and says the expedition passed through 'with soldiers.' Beat: fear made concrete — this is bigger than looting.

chapters.title: Soldiers of the Collector
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Armed men patrol the narrows ahead, turning back travelers. Theo runs the Marrow through a side channel at night, nearly losing the boat on submerged stakes. Beat: Theo's competence as identity — she is her mother's child whether she likes it or not.

chapters.title: The Shrine Island
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. They hide on a sacred island where a caretaker priest shelters them and speaks of 'the woman who wept but would not leave' — Adaeze visited weeks ago, asking about old trade routes. Beat: Theo hears her mother described as human for the first time in years.

chapters.title: Radio Silence, Broken
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. From the island's heights, Imani's repaired radio catches a fragment: Adaeze's voice, coded coordinates, and Voss's man cutting the transmission. She's alive — and captive by choice or force. Beat: hope and terror arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Middle Passage
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A brutal stretch of river: engine failure, Imani's malaria relapse, Theo carrying her ashore and facing, alone, the question of how far she'd go for a stranger. Beat: found family forming in extremis — Theo stays without being asked.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Camp
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Reconnaissance from a ridge: the 'expedition site' is a loading operation, crates of artifacts moving downriver under guard, Adaeze signing manifests at gunpoint-adjacent coercion. Beat: cold fury replacing grief — her mother is a hostage of paperwork.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Distance
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV (first time). Inside the camp, Adaeze catalogs every artifact by memory, planning to testify someday, keeping herself alive by being useful. She learns from a guard that a woman matching Theo's description was seen upriver. Beat: a mother's guilt meeting a mother's hope.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo slips into camp posing as a buyer's courier, and mother and daughter come face to face over a manifest table, playing strangers. Three sentences pass between them that carry twenty years. Beat: devastating restraint — reconciliation deferred by survival.

chapters.title: The Plan That Shouldn't Work
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. The three convene via stolen moments: flood the manifest records, trigger the monsoon evacuation, and let the river destroy the smuggling route while Imani's evidence reaches authorities downstream. Every step depends on timing against a storm that doesn't negotiate. Beat: fragile hope built on trust.

chapters.title: Voss Arrives
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Halvard Voss lands by seaplane to oversee the final shipment and smells sabotage immediately; he isolates Adaeze and reveals he knows exactly who Theo is. Beat: the villain makes it personal — leverage becomes love weaponized.

chapters.title: The Storm Makes Landfall
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The monsoon hits with full fury as the plan activates. Imani broadcasts the evidence; guards scatter; the river rises over the loading docks. Theo goes back for Adaeze against all sense. Beat: chaos as crucible — every theme converging.

chapters.title: The Choice of the River
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Climax. The camp floods; Voss tries to fly out with the most valuable pieces. Theo and Adaeze cut the seaplane loose rather than let it lift, choosing justice over the artifacts — and nearly drowning doing it. Voss escapes into the storm, but the evidence is already downstream. Beat: sacrifice as the price of integrity.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Water
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. The Marrow is gone; the three survive on the shrine island with the caretaker. Downstream, authorities intercept Voss's remaining shipments using Imani's ledger. Beat: exhaustion, grief for what was lost, quiet triumph for what wasn't.

chapters.title: Days, Not Miles
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Stranded together through the monsoon's tail, mother and daughter excavate nothing, fix nothing, measure nothing — they simply talk, for the first time since Theo was seventeen. Beat: the slow, unglamorous work of forgiveness.

chapters.title: What We Carry Out
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The rivers drop; a rescue launch arrives. Theo realizes she no longer wants to be the person who leaves first. Imani chooses to come with her — not because either needs rescuing, but because neither wants to drift alone. Beat: found family made explicit and chosen.

chapters.title: The Salt Passage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Epilogue, months later: Theo pilots a new boat, co-signed by Imani, toward a coastal dig where Adaeze consults honestly. The salt passage between river and sea — where fresh meets salt and neither wins — is where Theo finally feels at home. Beat: resolution; identity reconciled, family redefined, justice served outside the law's slow hands.
